lesson.subtitle: Lesson 27 -- Presentations I: Opening and Structure (Signposting)
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rafael Gasparelli Lima | Lesson 27 -- Opening the Presentation
lesson.grammar_point: discourse markers to structure a presentation: to begin with / first of all, moving on to, let's turn to, finally, to sum up

listenings.text: How do you start a presentation? Many people start with: Sorry, I'm a little nervous. Please don't. Your audience decides in the first minute if they want to listen. Here is a simple plan for a strong opening. First of all, say hello and thank people for coming. Second, say who you are, in one sentence. Then tell the audience the purpose of your talk: why are they here? After that, give a short overview of your main points. Three main points are perfect. Ten points are too many. Finally, tell people when they can ask questions. Do all this in about one minute. Remember: a good opening is not long. It's clear.

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for coming. My name is Daniel Visser, and I'm the head of logistics at Harbor Fresh Foods. The topic of today's presentation is how fruit travels from the farm to the supermarket. The purpose of this talk is to show you our rules for new suppliers. I have three main points. To begin with, I'll talk about temperature. Then I'll move on to packaging. Finally, I'll explain our delivery times. You can find all the details in the handout on your table. The talk is about twenty minutes, and there will be time for questions at the end. So, let's begin with temperature.

extra_audio.text: First of all, say hello and thank people for coming. Then, say your name and your role in one sentence. Next, tell the audience the topic and the purpose of the talk. After that, give a short overview of your three main points. Finally, say when people can ask questions, and begin with point one.
